votes.evidence:
Premise confirmed by tracing the call path.

1. `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:503-506` — `find_signal_implementation_run` calls `find_task_run(pr_url=..., branch=..., repository=...)` with no `team_id`, then does `if run is None or run.team_id != team_id: return None`. The team check is post-selection on a single row; there is no second lookup for the caller's team.

2. `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-64` — `find_task_run` filters only on `output__pr_url` + `task__repository__iexact` and orders by `terminal_rank, -created_at` then `.first()`. `webhooks.py:68-75` — the branch leg filters `branch` + `task__repository__iexact` + `state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True` and takes `.first()` under `TaskRun.Meta.ordering = ["-created_at"]` (`models.py:1146`). Neither leg has a `team_id` predicate, so a newer (or non-terminal vs terminal) row from any team wins.

3. The colliding row is creatable by another tenant: `Task.repository` is a free-form string validated only for `org/repo` shape (`models.py:258-263`, `presentation/serializers.py:600-609`; no check against the team's GitHub integration). `output.pr_url` is written by `set_task_run_output` scoped only to the writer's own run (`facade/api.py:2139-2154`; `_get_visible_run` at 1802-1804), with no attestation on `pr_url` (`_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS = {"pr_merged"}` at 1770). `TaskRun.branch` is client-supplied on run creation (`serializers.py:1690-1696`, `facade/api.py:992`).

4. Consequence for the owning team: `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191-200` — `run is None` → `_InboxCarveOut()` (no provenance). At `tasks.py:870-910` a bot-authored PR with `skip_reason` set and no `inbox_review` is skipped, and on head-changing actions `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` dismisses any standing approval with `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE`. So the victim team's self-driving PR silently loses its re-review, and its existing approval is retracted.

5. Existing test coverage `products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1287-1316` (`other_team` case) only asserts that a foreign-team run is rejected; no test creates a same-team run plus a newer foreign-team collider, so the shadowing path is untested.

Direction of failure is fail-safe (no cross-tenant approval is granted; the docstring's "no caller can accidentally bind a PR to another tenant's run" holds), which is why this is should_fix rather than must_fix: it is a cross-tenant denial of the self-driving re-review for the owning team, reachable by any account on another org that sets `repository`/`pr_url`/`branch` to match, with a one-line fix (filter `team_id` inside the lookup).
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) maybe `find_task_run` already scopes by team — it does not, both legs are global (`webhooks.py:41-56, 68-75`). (b) maybe another team cannot create a Task with the victim's repository slug — the only validation is the `org/repo` format (`models.py:258-263`, `serializers.py:600-609`); no integration-ownership check. (c) maybe `output.pr_url` cannot be set by a client — `set_output` (`views/api.py:1106-1121`) accepts arbitrary `pr_url` with only json_schema validation; only `pr_merged` is attested. (d) maybe the Stamphog caller falls back to a team-scoped lookup when the facade returns None — it does not; `tasks.py:199-200` returns an empty carve-out and the PR is skipped with approval retraction. (e) maybe the miss is harmless — it is not privilege escalation, but it does disable the owning team's re-review and dismisses its standing approval (`tasks.py:886-898`). Refutation fails; the finding is real, but its impact is a fail-safe cross-tenant denial, not a cross-tenant approval, so severity is should_fix rather than the claimed must_fix.

votes.evidence:
Code behaves as the finding says. `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504-506` calls `find_task_run(pr_url=..., branch=..., repository=...)` with no team filter and only afterwards does `if run is None or run.team_id != team_id: return None` — one global row is picked, then rejected, with no second attempt scoped to the caller's team. `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:41-56` (pr_url leg) filters `output__pr_url` + `task__repository__iexact` only, orders non-terminal first then `-created_at`, `.first()`; `webhooks.py:68-75` (branch leg) likewise has no `team_id`, and `TaskRun.Meta.ordering = ["-created_at"]` (`models.py:1144-1146`) makes the newest run win. So a newer run from another team with the same pr_url (or same repo+branch) shadows the owning team's run.

Reachability in production: (1) `Task.repository` is a free-form "org/repo" string, validated only for shape and lowercased (`presentation/serializers.py:600-609`); nothing binds it to the team's own GitHub installation, so any tenant can create tasks whose `repository` equals another tenant's repo. (2) `output.pr_url` is tenant-writable via the team-scoped `set_output` action (`presentation/views/api.py:1107-1118` -> `facade/api.py:2139-2154` `set_task_run_output`), so a tenant can put any PR URL into its own run. (3) Even without intent, the tasks webhook backstop `_record_run_pr_url` (`webhooks.py:159-181`) writes the incoming PR URL into whichever run wins the same global branch+repo lookup, so a branch-name collision in a shared repo binds team A's PR URL to team B's newer run automatically. (4) Shared repos across teams are an anticipated config: `_resolve_repo_config` (`stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:289-304`) documents "a later duplicate registration" and resolves oldest-wins. Consequence at the caller: `tasks.py:199-200` turns the None into `_InboxCarveOut()`, so the self-driving PR is treated as an ordinary bot PR and its re-review is skipped. Existing test `test_webhooks.py:1290-1320` ("other_team") only checks a lone other-team run returns None; no test has both teams' runs coexisting.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) Maybe the caller re-scopes — no, `tasks.py:191-200` does one call and fails closed. (b) Maybe `repository` is tied to the team's installation so no other tenant can share it — no, only format validation. (c) Maybe pr_url cannot land on another team's run — it can, via the tenant's own `set_output` or the webhook branch backstop. (d) Maybe the failure is harmless — it is fail-closed: the result is a skipped automated re-review, never a wrong approval, and the stale-approval retraction on head change is unaffected (`tasks.py:160-166` docstring). Also, in the shared-repo case `_resolve_repo_config` oldest-wins already means only one team's config governs the repo, which further narrows who can be affected. That is why this is should_fix, not must_fix: real cross-tenant interference with a narrow, non-destructive blast radius (denial of one tenant's automated re-review), and a one-line fix (push `team_id` into the `TaskRun` filters before ordering, keeping the post-check as defense in depth).
